name: MI300X vs H100, vLLM, Llama 3.1 405B FP8 TP8: output token throughput at 128-in/4096-out (MI300X wins 1.62x)
unit: output tok/s (aggregate over all in-flight requests)
methodology: Same aggregate closed-loop, infinite-rate, no-latency-constraint setup as the 70B pair. Llama 3.1 405B FP8, TP=8, input 128 / output 4096. AMD: 8x MI300X + EPYC, vllm-dev:20250112. NVIDIA: 8x H100 SXM + Xeon, trtllm-bench trtllm 0.16.0. OMITTED BY SOURCE: batch size, max_num_seqs, KV-cache dtype, GEMM tuning state, driver versions. Note the 405B FP8 weights fit on 8xMI300X but AMD notes FP16 405B does not fit on a single H100 node - the comparison is done entirely in FP8 to make that moot.
notes: DIRECTLY COMPARABLE to mi300x-vs-h100-vllm-llama31-405b-fp8-tp8-h100. This is the most striking ROCm-beats-CUDA number in the whole space: 3171 vs 1957 output tok/s = 1.62x for MI300X. Across the four 405B shapes in the same table MI300X wins all four (1.25x, 1.62x, 1.13x, 1.28x; geomean 1.31x). So on 70B MI300X is roughly at parity or slightly behind (geomean 0.94x) while on 405B it is clearly ahead (geomean 1.31x) - the crossover is not about CDNA vs Hopper per se but about the bandwidth-to-capacity balance at 8-way TP for large weights. Vendor-published with the same engine-mismatch and memory-capacity confound caveats as the 70B pair.
